en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
Pādukavagga 69.
The Training Rule on Low Seats.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, sitting on low seats, were teaching the Dhamma to those sitting on high seats.
Those monks who were of few desires... [and so forth]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
"How can the group-of-six monks, sitting on low seats, teach the Dhamma to those sitting on high seats?"... [and so forth]...
“Is it true, monks, that you sit on a low seat and teach the Dhamma to one sitting on a high seat?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, you foolish men, can you sit on a low seat and teach the Dhamma to one sitting on a high seat?
This, foolish men, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
Having rebuked them..."
Having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus:
“In the past, bhikkhus, in Bārāṇasī, a certain outcaste’s wife became pregnant.
Then, bhikkhus, that outcaste woman said this to her husband:”
“I am pregnant, noble son.
I wish to eat mangoes. “There are no mangoes;
it is not the season for mangoes.”
‘If I do not obtain [food], I shall die.
Now at that time, the king’s mango tree was always bearing fruit.
Then, monks, that outcaste went to where that mango tree was; having approached and climbed that mango tree, he remained hidden.
Then, monks, the king, together with the brahmin family priest, approached that mango tree. Having arrived, he sat down on a high seat and recited the mantras.
Then, monks, it occurred to that outcaste:
“How unrighteous this king is, in that he sits upon a high seat and recites the mantras!”
"And this brahmin is unrighteous, for he would have me sit on a low seat while teaching him the mantras as he sits on a high seat.
And I too am unrighteous, for I am stealing the king's mangoes for the sake of a woman.
All of this has been done in vain."
Right there they fall.
“Both do not know the goal;
both do not see the Dhamma.”
He who teaches the mantra,
and he who studies it unlawfully;
"Rice porridge has been eaten..."
With well-prepared meat as a sauce;
therefore, I do not speak against the Dhamma,
for the Dhamma is praised by the Noble Ones.
"Fie on that gain of wealth,
O brahmin, and fie on that gain of fame,
which is a livelihood dependent on a state of ruin!"
Or by practicing unrighteousness.
Wander forth, Great Brahmā,
even while other beings are cooking [their food].
"Do not practice unrighteousness;
do not shatter us like this jar!
Even then, monks, it was unpleasant for me to recite the mantra while seated on a high seat for one seated on a low seat.
How much more so now, monks, would it not be disagreeable for one sitting on a high seat to teach the Dhamma to one sitting on a low seat?
This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:
“The training is to be observed: ‘I shall not teach the Dhamma while sitting on a low seat to one who is not ill and is sitting on a high seat.
One should not teach the Dhamma while sitting on a low seat to one who is not ill and is sitting on a high seat.
Whoever, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma while sitting on a low seat to one who is not ill and is sitting on a high seat, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).”
There is no offense if it was unintentional … [and so on] … for one who is a beginner.
The ninth training rule is concluded.
